set.approach: From Valdez drive up Thompson Pass and leave the car at the large pullout beside Odyssey Lake, level with the 27-mile post. Cross the road to the streambed and follow it up until the crag appears on the left. The line climbs a crack set in a corner, clips a bolt, pulls a small roof, and ends up the short face over it.

review.notes: Approach from the crag page; route line from the route page. Two-bolt anchor only, no descent stated.

set.approach: The Mendenhall Towers stand north of Juneau and can be reached by helicopter from town; the other ways are to ski north along Blackerby Ridge toward the glacier's northern fork, or to climb the glacier itself from the West Glacier trail. The glacier below The Curtain has the largest flat stretch beneath the towers and serves as the landing and camp spot for south-side routes, which need basic glacier travel skills. Inside Passage lies in the centre of the main wall, starting up a splitting right-facing corner; the moat at the foot of the wall has to be crossed from the snow.
set.descent_text: Rappel back to camp down the Iron Curtain line. To find its anchors, head west along the summit scramble to the large cairn of blocks that marks the top of the Iron Curtain; the rappels are mostly done with two ropes. The alternative is to continue to the Main Tower or the Fourth Tower summit and follow the descent from those.

review.notes: Approach from Towers and Curtain pages and route Location; descent from the Curtain wall page (route page gives none).

Looking from the Fourth Tower's south side, find the broad couloir descending; the buttress forming its left edge holds The Mammoth, on a crack system running from the glacier up to the right of a feature shaped like a mammoth's trunk.
set.descent_text: Rappel the bolted rappel line down the route, keeping the ropes out of the cracks in the upper part.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page; Towers/Curtain pages for access (counts omitted).

set.approach: The 5390 massif sits in the middle of Baranof Island east of Sitka and is remote. One approach begins where the gate blocks Sawmill Creek Road, and continues by bike or on foot to an old gravel pit beyond the hatchery, then follows flagging to the southern flank of Cross Mountain and links a chain of ridges to the massif; allow a full day. A shorter approach rides the road to Green Lake, crosses the lake by kayak, and climbs flagged ground to the ridge and across the alpine. Parties camp on the level snow shelf beneath the west face, and the routes are spread along the foot of that face from camp. All That for a Hand Crack? is on the southernmost formation of the west face, to the right of Fossilized Potential. It starts up a diagonal, left-leaning double crack.

review.notes: Approach from massif and west face pages; start from route page. Page mentions only a snow descent line, not enough for a descent text.

set.descent_text: Walk off: head south across the snow, skirting the east side of the 5390 summit to the saddle, then west down to camp, picking a way through any crevasses in the col.

set.approach: Angstroms is a large crag of soft, crumbly rock, found by driving north on the Kougarok road a little beyond Bear Mountain. Goshawk is on the left side of the crag, following a flake on the south face.

review.notes: Approach from the crag page; start from the route Location. Only top-rope bolts mentioned, no descent.

set.approach: From Haines head out the highway and park where the guardrail ends just past the 17 mile sign. Drop into the ditch, follow the creek past the culvert, and take the flagged trail up into the woods to a boulder field. For Bear Spray Wall cross the boulder field angling up and right, then follow the flagged trail past three small chossy cliffs to the wall. The route starts at the first obvious trad line on arriving at the wall, as for Spray Some on Yourself, going up a ramp to the left and out of an alcove, then follows a crack to the right.

review.notes: Approach from 17 Mile and Bear Spray Wall pages; start from route text. No descent stated.

set.approach: From Haines head out the highway and park where the guardrail ends just past the 17 mile sign. Drop into the ditch, follow the creek past the culvert, and take the flagged trail up into the woods to a boulder field. For Bear Spray Wall cross the boulder field angling up and right, then follow the flagged trail past three small chossy cliffs to the wall. It is the first trad line that heads directly upward when you arrive at the wall: a short ramp up and left leads to an alcove, then the line goes straight up into the hand crack.

review.notes: Approach from 17 Mile and Bear Spray Wall pages; start from the route page. Rap ring anchor only, no descent stated.

set.approach: Drive into Red Rock Canyon about halfway, to the bend where the big pile of red debris nears the road, and park in any of the pullouts after it. Look east for the prominent ridge that reaches the canyon floor with little brush, and hike it to the rim. Cross the tundra plateau from the west rim to the east rim; the alpine lake below Canwell Peak comes into view, and the crag sits just south, nearer the peak, at the top of the plateau. 3 Bears is the left crack on the last vertical wall, downhill and to the right.

review.notes: Approach from crag page; start from route Location. No descent stated.

set.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. Chicken Rock is a smaller rock that resembles a chicken, set above and to the right of the Southeast Buttress and below and to the right of the East Tower. Corner is the large corner system high on the formation's left side, as seen walking up to the rock.

review.notes: Approach from Prindle and Chicken Rock pages and route Location; walk-off from the route page, consistent with the rock page noting easy descents.

set.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. Birthday on the Sheep Trail takes the big weakness in the middle of the Main Wall, to the left of the Keyhole and the bear cave; hiking on around the slabby apron means you have overshot it. It starts just right of the loose rock that forms the obvious weakness.
set.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right, down toward the East Tower and back to camp.

review.notes: Approach from Prindle page and route text; descent from the route page only.

set.approach: Mount Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that favours a high-clearance 4x4, followed by a long hike in to the base of the main walls. Godiva is a variation on the finish of Ghirardelli: as you come to the top of its grass gully, head right of the tower to a single-bolt anchor, which is the start. The line follows a distinct ledge, with the wall dropping off to its right.

review.notes: Approach from Prindle page and route Location. Route ends scrambling to the summit; no descent stated.

set.approach: Little Switzerland on the Pika Glacier is reached by air taxi from Talkeetna. From the landing strip, ski or snowshoe up the glacier to Crown Jewel, the wide formation beside the Munchkin and the Royal Tower. The route begins from the saddle between Crown Jewel and the Royal Tower, between the Pika and Crown glaciers, on the Crown Jewel flank, at a buttress with a large hanging glacier on its west side. Cross the bergschrund and angle up and right on steepening snow to the rock below a big right-facing corner.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route rather than downclimbing the snow and crossing the bergschrund again.

review.notes: Approach from Little Switzerland and Crown Jewel pages and route text; rappel from the route page only.

set.approach: Devil's Thumb is reached by helicopter from Petersburg or by boat and foot from the coast. This route is on the south side. The approach comes up from the Cauldron beneath it, following a ramp system in the rock beside the southern icefall's west edge, a spot that suits a helicopter drop. A second way is to descend from the upper base camp, which passes under some objective hazard. Either way, cross the upper pocket glacier to the lower-angle rock ridge that leads to the south pillar, mostly third and fourth class with a little fifth. The first pitch begins from the notch under the south pillar.
set.descent_text: Descend the route by rappel, using the face below the traverse until you re-enter the large corner system.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page and the Devil's Thumb page.

set.approach: Park at Black Rapids Lodge, or at the Richardson Highway pullout at mile 227, and take the trail from the lodge to the pipeline cut. Walk south along the cut to Gunnysack Creek and continue into the canyon. The line is on one of the few outcrops along Gunnysack's south ridge; search for an arete that drops the whole way from the canyon rim.
set.descent_text: Walk off by bushwhacking across to the neighbouring hill, then take the trails back down to Gunnysack.

review.notes: Approach from the creek page and route Location; walk-off from the route page only.

set.approach: Lion's Head is a big igneous intrusion overlooking the Matanuska Glacier, reached from a pullout off the Glenn Highway near the communications tower. From the pullout take the trail, and cut right where it steepens. Sidehill around to the talus and descend along the cliff edge. The route climbs the west-facing cliff above Coyote Creek and starts below a clean face, taking the left line of the two weaknesses.

review.notes: Approach from area page and route Location. No descent stated.

set.approach: From Palmer take North Palmer Fishhook Road to the Mother Lode Lodge switchback, then Archangel Road past the bridge to the Reed Lakes trailhead. The trail winds up to an abandoned cabin, where the climbing in the basin begins. Mile High Wall is approached by climbing the drainage that comes down from the west to the trail connecting the two lakes. Main Wall is at the centre of the cliff, right of the Shield and below the Diving Board. Air Sex Society starts on the slab below the dihedral.

review.notes: Approach from Reed Lakes, Mile High Wall and Main Wall pages; start from route Location. No descent stated.

Main Wall is at the centre of the cliff, right of the Shield and below the Diving Board. Moon Pilot begins in a short, low-angle, left-facing dihedral leading to a small ledge.
set.descent_text: Walk off, or rappel over the large roof from the separate two-bolt anchor that belongs to a different route.

review.notes: Approach from area pages; start and descent from the route page.

set.approach: The wall stands at the north end of the New Harbor at Valdez. Leave the vehicle just to the south of it, out of the way of fishing activity. Harbor Fever is among the first vertical cracks you meet counting from the wall's right end.
set.descent_text: Rappel off the alders, or walk off along the main trail.

review.notes: Approach from the wall page and route Location; descent from the route page.

set.approach: The Trolls are summits just south of the Throne in Little Switzerland, in Denali National Park, reached by air taxi from Talkeetna. Approach North Troll via the glacier from the landing strip. The route follows the northeast ridge and then the north face.

review.notes: Approach from North Troll and Little Switzerland pages; route page is nearly empty and gives no descent.

set.approach: From the Reed Lakes lot, walk to the former building site, short of Nugget Boulder and the Snowbird slab. Then take the path bearing left up the drainage, past the Snowbird mine on your right, and keep going up the bowls to the pass. The Snowbird Glacier lies below the pass, and the Nunatak is the small formation beside it. Walk to the foot of the conspicuous dihedral on the east face's left side, which is really a gully.
set.descent_text: Retrace the summit scramble to the top of the third pitch, where rappel slings are found on blocks, and scramble south from there past a second sling station; both are options, and the scramble down is loose, so keep your partner out from below.

review.notes: Approach from Nunatak and Glacier Creek pages and route Location; descent from the route page only.
